  1. defLax825748.ConvergentSeries

    Convergent commutative power series

    A real power series in ddd commuting variables is convergent if its coefficients admit a geometric bound ∣fI∣≤αC∣I∣|f_I|\leq\alpha C^{|I|}∣fI​∣≤αC∣I∣ with α,C>0\alpha,C>0α,C>0. For finitely many variables this is equivalent to absolute convergence on a neighborhood of the origin. Dimension zero is included.

  2. defLax825748.AnalyticRepresentations

    Analytic differential representations

    A differential representation is analytic if its output series and every coefficient of each of its vector fields converge near the origin. Its generated coefficient at a word www is the constant term of hμwh\mu whμw, with the vector fields acting on the right in the order of the letters. A series is analytically produced if such a representation exists in some finite dimension, including dimension zero.

    Convergence of the vector fields is required explicitly. It is used in the proof and in the interpretation by analytic systems, although omitted from the printed Definition 1.

  3. defLax825748.Series

    Noncommutative series and polynomial residuals

    For an alphabet XXX, a series is a function X∗→RX^*\to\mathbb RX∗→R and a polynomial is a finite real linear combination of words. Polynomial multiplication is concatenation. The pairing is (S,P)=∑wPwSw(S,P)=\sum_w P_w S_w(S,P)=∑w​Pw​Sw​.

    The two residuals are (S∘P,w)=(S,Pw)(S\circ P,w)=(S,Pw)(S∘P,w)=(S,Pw) and (P∘S,w)=(S,wP)(P\circ S,w)=(S,wP)(P∘S,w)=(S,wP). The empty word is the monoid identity. Agreement below degree NNN means equality at every word of length less than NNN.

  4. defLax825748.LieRank

    Lie polynomials and Lie rank

    The Lie polynomials form the Lie subalgebra of R⟨X⟩\mathbb R\langle X\rangleR⟨X⟩ generated by the letters, with bracket [P,Q]=PQ−QP[P,Q]=PQ-QP[P,Q]=PQ−QP. The Lie residual space of ggg is the linear span of the series P∘gP\circ gP∘g for Lie polynomials PPP. The assertion that ggg has Lie rank ddd includes finite dimensionality; in particular an infinite-dimensional space never has rank zero by convention.

  5. def✓Lax825748.ConvergenceHypothesis

    The convergence hypothesis on Lie polynomials

    Condition (C) requires that, for every finite ordered family of Lie polynomials P1,…,PqP_1,\ldots,P_qP1​,…,Pq​, there are α,C>0\alpha,C>0α,C>0 such that

    ∣(g,P1i1⋯Pqiq)∣≤αC∣I∣I!.|(g,P_1^{i_1}\cdots P_q^{i_q})|\leq\alpha C^{|I|}I!.∣(g,P1i1​​⋯Pqiq​​)∣≤αC∣I∣I!.

    The constants may depend on the family, but not on the exponents.

    The inequalities I!≤∣I∣!≤q∣I∣I!I!\leq |I|!\leq q^{|I|}I!I!≤∣I∣!≤q∣I∣I! show that replacing I!I!I! by ∣I∣!|I|!∣I∣! gives the same condition. Empty families are allowed.

  6. thm✓Lax825748.Realization

    Local analytic realization of generating series

    For a finite alphabet, a real noncommutative series admits an analytic differential representation if and only if it has finite Lie rank and satisfies (C). If its Lie rank is ddd, a representation of dimension exactly ddd exists.

    The realization is obtained in the normalized residual coordinates Ti=g∘Qi−(g,Qi)T_i=g\circ Q_i-(g,Q_i)Ti​=g∘Qi​−(g,Qi​). Convergence of the output and of the vector-field coefficients follows from their convergent coordinate expansions.

  7. thm✓Lax825748.Minimality

    Lie rank is the least analytic realization dimension

    A series has Lie rank ddd and satisfies (C) if and only if ddd is the least dimension of its analytic differential representations. The least dimension is attained. Constant series are included with dimension zero.

    25 (HasLieRank g d ∧ ConvergenceHypothesis.Holds g) ↔ IsLeastDimension g d

  8. thm✓Lax825748.Uniqueness

    Analytic equivalence of minimal realizations

    Two analytic differential representations of a series of Lie rank ddd, both of dimension ddd, are related by an analytic change of coordinates fixing the origin. This change sends the first output to the second and intertwines the action of every word on every state series. Its inverse is also convergent and formally continuous.

  9. def✓Lax825748.Shuffle

    Shuffle multiplication

    The coefficient of www in the shuffle of SSS and TTT is the sum of S(w∣I)T(w∣Ic)S(w|I)T(w|I^c)S(w∣I)T(w∣Ic) over subsets of the positions of www. Repeated letters retain their multiplicities. This product is associative and commutative, with unit the series supported at the empty word. No concatenation product on series is used here.

  10. thm✓Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities

    Coproduct and shuffle identities

    Lemmas 1–5. The ppp-fold coproduct assigns each position of a word to one of ppp tensor factors. Tensor polynomials are represented by finite linear combinations of ppp-tuples of words. Its value on a letter is the sum of the ppp placements of that letter, and Lie polynomials are primitive.

    Pairing with this coproduct computes the shuffle product. Letter residuals are derivations. A shuffle product of iii zero-constant series vanishes on a product of fewer than iii Lie polynomials. For equal numbers of factors, the pairing is the sum over permutations of pairwise evaluations.

    For normalized coordinate series, equal-degree monomials have diagonal pairing I!=∏iIi!I!=\prod_i I_i!I!=∏i​Ii​! and off-diagonal pairing zero. This corrects the printed ∣I∣!|I|!∣I∣! in Lemma 5(ii).

  11. thm✓Lax825748.PBW

    Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt for Lie polynomials

    Given any totally ordered basis of the Lie polynomials, the nondecreasing products of its basis elements, including the empty product, form a basis of the concatenation algebra R⟨X⟩\mathbb R\langle X\rangleR⟨X⟩. Linear independence and spanning are stated separately in the conjunction.

  12. thm✓Lax825748.FactorialEstimate

    Factorial estimates for iterated analytic vector fields

    Suppose the output and all vector-field coefficients admit the same bound αC∣I∣\alpha C^{|I|}αC∣I∣, where α,C>0\alpha,C>0α,C>0. For a word of length ppp, its generated coefficient has absolute value at most α(2dαC)pp!\alpha(2d\alpha C)^p p!α(2dαC)pp!. Consequently every analytic representation on a finite alphabet has a uniform factorial bound on its word coefficients.

    The central binomial estimate used in the majorant calculation is (2pp)≤4p\binom{2p}{p}\leq 4^p(p2p​)≤4p, rather than the printed 2p2^p2p.

  13. thm✓Lax825748.NecessaryConvergence

    Analytic representations satisfy the convergence hypothesis

    The generating series of an analytic differential representation satisfies condition (C). A finite family of Lie polynomials acts by analytic vector fields. Applying the factorial estimate to these new fields, and comparing the total factorial with the product of factorials, gives the assertion.

  14. thm✓Lax825748.Annihilator

    Formal coordinates on the annihilator of a Lie subalgebra

    Proposition 1. Let L0L_0L0​ be a Lie subalgebra of the Lie polynomials and let P1,…,PdP_1,\ldots,P_dP1​,…,Pd​ represent a basis modulo L0L_0L0​. Set J=R⟨X⟩L0J=\mathbb R\langle X\rangle L_0J=R⟨X⟩L0​. If the zero-constant series SiS_iSi​ vanish on JJJ and satisfy (Si,Pj)=δij(S_i,P_j)=\delta_{ij}(Si​,Pj​)=δij​, substitution of the SiS_iSi​ into commutative formal series is a bijection onto J⊥J^\perpJ⊥.

    Substitution is defined coefficient by coefficient using a finite truncation: at a word of length nnn, only monomials of degree at most nnn contribute. There exist such coordinates dual to the degree-one PBW monomials. For these coordinates the coefficient of SIS^ISI in T∈J⊥T\in J^\perpT∈J⊥ is (T,PI)/I!(T,P^I)/I!(T,PI)/I!. The annihilator is closed under the shuffle and all right residuals.

    31
    32noncomputable def generatedIdeal {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) :
    33 Ideal (NCPolynomial X) :=
    34 Ideal.span {P | ∃ k : K, P = k.val.val}
    35
    36def InAnnihilator {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) (S : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
    37 ∀ P ∈ generatedIdeal K, pairing S P = 0
    38
    39def IsComplement {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    40 (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) : Prop :=
    41 LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => K.toSubmodule.mkQ (P i)) ∧
    42 Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => K.toSubmodule.mkQ (P i)) = ⊤
    43
    44def IsCoordinateFamily {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    45 (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) : Prop :=
    46 (∀ i, S i 1 = 0) ∧ (∀ i, InAnnihilator K (S i)) ∧
    47 ∀ i j, pairing (S i) (P j).val = if i = j then 1 else 0

    49noncomputable def substituteShuffle {X : Type} {d : ℕ}
    50 (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (f : StateSeries d) : NCSeries X :=
    51 fun w => (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff
    52 (MvPowerSeries.truncTotal (w.toList.length + 1) f)).sum
    53 fun I a => a * shuffleMonomial S I w
    54
    55def IsPBWCoordinateFamily {X : Type} {d : ℕ}
    56 (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) : Prop :=
    57 ∀ i (I : Fin d →₀ ℕ),
    58 pairing (S i) (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I) =
    59 if I = Finsupp.single i 1 then 1 else 0
    60
    61axiom coordinates_exist {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    62 (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P) :
    63 ∃ S : Fin d → NCSeries X, IsCoordinateFamily K P S ∧ IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S

    66 (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P)
    67 (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (hS : IsCoordinateFamily K P S) :

    71 (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P)
    72 (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (hS : IsCoordinateFamily K P S)
    73 (hPBW : IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S) (T : NCSeries X) (hT : InAnnihilator K T) :
    74 ∃ f : StateSeries d, substituteShuffle S f = T ∧
    75 ∀ I : Fin d →₀ ℕ, MvPowerSeries.coeff I f =
    76 pairing T (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I) / (multiFactorial I : ℝ)
    77
    78axiom closed_shuffle {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    79 (S T : NCSeries X) (hS : InAnnihilator K S) (hT : InAnnihilator K T) :
    80 InAnnihilator K (shuffle S T)

    83 (S : NCSeries X) (hS : InAnnihilator K S) (P : NCPolynomial X) :
    84 InAnnihilator K (rightResidual S P)

  17. thm✓Lax825748.AnalyticChanges

    Analytic changes of coordinates

    An analytic change of coordinates is a formally continuous real algebra automorphism fixing the origin whose coordinate images, in both directions, are convergent power series.

    The analytic inverse function theorem implies that a formal change of coordinates with convergent coordinate images has convergent inverse images. This is the implicit function theorem used in part b) of the paper.
